text:
maya (PM): quick sync — i'm drafting a compact decision rubric to land GA for the next inference release. need buy-in on minimal SLAs, docs + runbooks, oncall coverage, and pricing guardrails. can folks call out hard blockers?
noah (Eng): +1. main technical risk is fallback behavior when a quantized model spikes latency. we should define an explicit fallback chain and a max-fallback-time SLA.
sam (SRE): prefer concrete numbers rather than fuzzy terms. proposal: P99 <= 300ms for 8k context on dedicated, P95 <= 120ms for hosted. if breach >5min across customers, auto-escalate to oncall.
alex (FinOps): pricing implication — if we promise those P99s we'll need reserved capacity tiers. recommend a burst policy with metered overage so we don't land on huge fixed costs. also need a doc table mapping SLA tier -> expected $/token delta.
lucy (Support): docs/runbooks should include triage steps for latency vs error vs quality regressions. also want a canned customer message for degradations. can we commit to an RTO for degraded mode (eg: 15m to enable reduced-quality fallback)?
noah (Eng): agree on fallback chain: 1) lightweight quantized variant -> 2) shorter context window -> 3) cached prefix responses -> 4) degraded-quality model (best-effort). add circuit-breaker: if fallback chain used >10% of requests in 10m, divert to dedicated pool and alert.
maya (PM): ok items to capture in GA rubric: SLA numbers, fallback chain, monitoring signals, runbook snippets, support playbooks, pricing tiers, rollouts/canaries, and opt-out/security constraints. any objections?
sam (SRE): monitoring signals list: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail error rate, token throughput, cache hit ratio, fallback-rate, queue depth, model-load-time. we need dashboards for each signal and an alert playbook mapping severity -> pager escalation.
alex (FinOps): for pricing tiers: Free/Starter/Reserved. Starter should include throttled burst (50% of reserved qps) and Reserved gets priority routing + tighter SLA. we should include a sample cost calculator in docs for common qps patterns.
lucy (Support): runbook sections: quick checks (is host healthy, recent deploys?), mitigation steps (enable cache, switch to reserved bucket), communication templates. also need a training doc for L2 on how to read the latency/kv-cache charts.
noah (Eng): small nit: for the circuit-breaker thresholds we should baseline from canary data. propose we hold the final numbers until we have 72h of canary telemetry.
maya (PM): good. plan: i'll draft the GA rubric doc with placeholders for the numbers sam/noah will fill after canary. action owners: maya -> doc skeleton, noah -> fallback and circuit-breaker final thresholds, sam -> alert mappings + dashboards, alex -> pricing delta table + cost calc, lucy -> support playbook + templates.
ops-bot: maya created document: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/GA-RUBRIC-286 (assigned) :white_check_mark:
maya (PM): timeline suggestion — draft by EOD Wednesday, canary starts Thursday, collect 72h telemetry, finalize by following Tuesday. flag anything unrealistic.
alex (FinOps): timeline ok but need cost model from canary within 48h of start to validate pricing tiers.
sam (SRE): agree. also request a staged alerting plan: enable low-sensitivity alerts in canary, then tighten during ramp.
lucy (Support): i'll prepare 2 sample customer comms (degradation + GA onboarding checklist) by Monday.
noah (Eng): i'll add a quick test harness for fallback chain simulation so we can stress the thresholds before canary. should land a PR tonight.
maya (PM): thanks all — i'll ping when draft is up. small ask: put any constraints (legal/compliance, data residency) in the doc too so private deployment customers are covered. :pray:
